newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR EXTENDS LOSSES ON U.S. UNIT.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR EXTENDS LOSSES ON U.S. UNIT.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar extended its losses on the U.S. dollar on Tuesday amid continued pressure but managed to post gains against other hard currencies, dealers said.

"We continued seeing a slide of the (Zimbabwe) dollar and I think everyone was just holding on to what little they had instead of letting it into the market," a trader said at the close of interbank trade.
"The Reserve Bank has been sitting on the sidelines since last week. Maybe we haven't reached the levels they want the exchange rate to be (at)," he added.
"The indications are that tomorrow the Zimbabwe dollar will continue falling," said another trader.
Some of the dealers expressed concern that the local unit was falling rather too rapidly and said this might hurt local importers.
"I'm not worried about the depreciation, but the rate of depreciation is of major concern," said one.
The local unit ended Tuesday at 11.0700/0800 against the U.S. dollar from Monday's 11.0575/0675 but edged up on the rand to 2.4700/4800 from 2.5000/5200.
It was also quoted stronger against sterling at 17.8700/9100 compared to 17.9200/9400 and was at 6.5000/5100 versus the mark from 6.5300/5500.
